collection_summary: This instance is a source-defined top-k geography ranking. It uses Britannica's ranked article on the world's largest islands and stages the first 20 islands by area as a top_k benchmark item.
source_coverage_notes: The cited Britannica page explicitly lists the 10 largest islands and then the next 15 largest islands. This staged table keeps the first 20 entries from that 25-entry source list. No rows were supplemented from other sources, and no row was generated from parametric knowledge. The claim is source-defined because area values and some rank boundaries vary modestly across published geographic references.
decision_log: Chose this instance to fill the currently empty top_k category with a stable, broadly knowable geography task. Britannica was selected as a compact third-party reference with explicit ranking and numeric area values. The LLM-facing title does not name Britannica, but the draft db_analog and curation record preserve the source-defined nature of the ground truth. Set operation_type=projection as the closest UI-supported coarse operation for a single-source ranked projection; the top-k semantics are represented by query_category=top_k and the ORDER BY/LIMIT db_analog. No proposed_supplements were needed because the source already supplies more than the requested top 20.
normalization_decisions: Area values were normalized to bare integer square kilometers by removing commas and unit words. The parenthetical location text after each island name was normalized into the Region column. Island names use Britannica's display names, with alternate names omitted unless Britannica used them as the main display form. The primary key is Island rather than Rank so rank errors are evaluated as non-key cell errors rather than changing row identity.
open_questions: Before registration, decide whether source-defined Britannica values are acceptable for a top_k task where other references, such as Wikipedia, report slightly different areas and may swap the order of nearby ranks. If cross-source consensus is preferred, this instance should be audited against a second ranked geography source before registration.
